newsitem.title: USA: Banc One's Oklahoma deal seen fitting its strategy.
newsitem.headline: Banc One's Oklahoma deal seen fitting its strategy.

text.p: Banc One Corp's planned acquisition of Liberty Bancorp Inc of Oklahoma for about $546 million in stock is a good strategic move for the Columbus, Ohio-based bank, analysts said Monday.

"It's an opportunistic deal for (Banc One)," Nancy Bush, an analyst with Brown Brothers Harriman. "They had a very, very small presence in Oklahoma -- (about) $600 million in assets, which made them an also-ran in the state -- and they take it up to number two" in Oklahoma with the Liberty deal.
"Banc One always has a goal of being (number) one, two or three in a market, so strategically, I think it does fit," Joseph Duwan, an analyst with Keefe Bruyette & Woods, said.

Bush and Stifel Nicolaus's Joseph Stieven said the price was reasonable. Duwan said Banc One was paying "a pretty full price" but added that Banc One expected to prune expenses and sees revenue opportunities, particularly in loan generation.
"They're buying a very good franchise in Liberty," Stieven said. "They don't have to pay a lot of money to get very significant market share... (and) Oklahoma is a great market."
Bush said she expected more acquisition news from Banc One.
"(Liberty) is not the big deal everybody's been looking for," she said. "I don't think this will be enough to alleviate the speculation that there is another larger deal coming up in '97."

Bush said she expected the Liberty acquisition to lower Banc One's 1997 earnings slightly and have no effect in 1998. But Duwan said he saw no impact in 1997 and believed the deal would be modestly accretive for Banc One in 1998.
Banc One, 10th largest in the U.S., had assets of $98.6 billion and Liberty had about $2.9 billion at September 30.
